The Express 5 adapter of the EGRADX server SDK for Node. It does what the Java SDK's request filters and exception handler do.

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `requestContext()` | Register first. Gives every request an id (the caller's `X-Request-ID` or `X-Trace-Id` when well-formed, else a UUID), returns it in `X-Request-ID`, and runs the request inside the EGRADX context, with the id in `@babulvaibhav/egradx-observability`'s logging context too (Java's MDC), so log lines and the work the request hands off (notifications, audit records) carry it. The client's address is recorded as Java writes it (`javaHostAddress()`), so audit records and attempt limits read the same from either SDK. |
| `authenticate({ verifier, resolve? })` | Makes the bearer token's caller the context's user; `resolve` looks the caller up afresh (`@babulvaibhav/egradx-auth` provides one). A request without a token, or with a refused one, continues anonymous. |
| `requireAuthenticated()` | 401 `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` without a token, 401 `SESSION_EXPIRED` with a refused one, as Java's `EgradxAuthenticationEntryPoint`. |
| `currentUser()`, `signedInUser()` | The caller of the current request. |
| `notFound()`, `errorHandler()` | Register last. Every failure becomes the contract's error envelope: `EgradxError`s with their status and code, malformed JSON as 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, anything unexpected as 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` (logged, revealing nothing). |

Tested with Express 5 only, including that the context survives `express.json()` and `await`.

## Functions

### authenticate()

```ts
function authenticate(options): RequestHandler;
```

Reads `Authorization: Bearer …` and, when the token verifies, makes the caller the context's user.
A request without a token, or with a refused one, continues anonymous: whether that is allowed is
decided per route by `requireAuthenticated()` (or the application's own check). Register after
`requestContext()`.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`AuthenticateOptions`](#authenticateoptions) |

#### Returns

`RequestHandler`

***

### errorHandler()

```ts
function errorHandler(options?): ErrorRequestHandler;
```

Register last. Turns every failure into the error envelope (contracts/schemas/error.json):
EgradxErrors with their status and code; malformed JSON as 400 INVALID_REQUEST; other HTTP errors
from Express or its body parsers with their status and the generic code for it; anything else as
500 INTERNAL_ERROR, logged, with a message that reveals nothing.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`ErrorHandlerOptions`](#errorhandleroptions) |

#### Returns

`ErrorRequestHandler`

***

### javaHostAddress()

```ts
function javaHostAddress(address): string;
```

An address as Java's InetAddress.getHostAddress writes it, so audit records and attempt limits read the
same whichever SDK served the request: an IPv4 client on a dual-stack socket as plain IPv4
(`::ffff:127.0.0.1` → `127.0.0.1`), IPv6 as eight groups without compression or leading zeros
(`::1` → `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1`), a zone kept. Anything unparseable is returned unchanged.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `address` | `string` |

#### Returns

`string`

***

function notFound(): RequestHandler;

`RequestHandler`

### requestContext()

```ts
function requestContext(options?): RequestHandler;
```

Register first. Gives every request an id (the caller's when well-formed, else a new UUID), returns
it in X-Request-ID before anything else runs (so error responses and streams carry it), and runs the
rest of the request inside the EGRADX request context that `currentContext()` and the other
middleware read. The Node counterpart of the Java SDK's EgradxRequestCorrelationFilter.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`RequestContextOptions`](#requestcontextoptions) |

#### Returns

`RequestHandler`

***

### requireAuthenticated()

```ts
function requireAuthenticated(): RequestHandler;
```

401 unless the request has a signed-in caller: SESSION_EXPIRED when a token was presented and
refused (the client should refresh or sign in again), NOT_AUTHENTICATED when there was none.
The same answers as the Java SDK's EgradxAuthenticationEntryPoint.

#### Returns

`RequestHandler`

***

### signedInUser()

```ts
function signedInUser(): EgradxUserTokenContext;
```

The signed-in caller, or an AuthenticationException: for handlers behind `requireAuthenticated()`.

#### Returns

[`EgradxUserTokenContext`](#egradxusertokencontext)
